body: Actually, what I see is that application startup events are invoked before any `MockSupport` methods are called, so probably this is fired before all our observer mocking setup.

Yes, startup events are fired by `QuarkusTestExtension` in:

```java
            runningQuarkusApplication = startupAction.run();
```

Way before we do the mock setup in before/after methods.

> Actually, what I see is that application startup events are invoked before any `MockSupport` methods are called, so probably this is fired before all our observer mocking setup.

Right, mocking doesn't really come into play with the events, so I don't think we can do much here...

> Right, mocking doesn't really come into play with the events, so I don't think we can do much here...

According to @mkouba mocking a bean is supposed to disable all its observer methods.

Hm... I don't think that is the case because IIRC, all mocking does under the hood is add a field to the normal scoped bean that can be used as the "target" instead of the actual instance of the bean.
But there might be something I am missing

Well, I think the logical intuitive behaviour is:

- For `@Mock`, overriding the event method should hijack the event, just like overriding other methods override behaviour. In practice, if I do that, _both_ methods get called (supertype and mock type). Yeah, that's just super weird.
- For `@InjectMock`, the event method should be a noop just like very other bean method, at least until we can define what behaviour it should have with `Mockito`. In practice, it's not.

So this is not working according to intuition.

> > Right, mocking doesn't really come into play with the events, so I don't think we can do much here...
> 
> According to @mkouba mocking a bean is supposed to disable all its observer methods.

It does but `StartupEvent` is a bit special because it's fired before the mock is created. It's fired when the app starts.
So is there a way forward @mkouba ?
My workaround is to use PostConstruct/PreDestroy with trivial usage of the bean in question in the QuarkusApplication run.
Maybe we just need some way to disable StartupEvent or @Startup beans being created when running tests?
